The Nasdaq-100 Is Outperforming Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Alphabet, and Tesla This Year. Here's My Favorite Low-Cost ETF to Buy the Dip.

GOOG

TSLA

The market's leadership has changed. Many of the mega-ap growth stocks that drove the indexes to new heights in recent years are now lagging.

The Nasdaq-100, which is the 100 largest non-financial stocks in the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC), is up 12.4% year-to-date (YTD) at the time of this writing. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) have produced smaller gains, while Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) are down YTD. This means that six "Magnificent Seven" stocks are underperforming the Nasdaq-100 YTD -- the only exception being Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's why the Vanguard Morningstar Mega Cap Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: MGK) is an excellent low-cost way to buy the dip on top growth stocks.

Image source: Getty Images.
The Mega Cap Growth ETF has 67.6% in 10 stocks

The Mega Cap Growth ETF is essentially a more concentrated version of the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: VUG). The Mega Cap ETF has 52 holdings compared to 135 for the Growth ETF. The expense ratio of the Mega Cap ETF is 0.05% -- only slightly higher than the Growth ETF's 0.03% expense ratio. It's worth noting that 0.03% is the lowest you'll find for any ETF. The largest ETF by net assets in the world is the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF, which also has a 0.03% expense ratio.

AAPL data by YCharts

Because of the sheer size of the largest U.S. companies, the top 10 holdings in the Mega Cap Growth ETF make up a staggering 67.6% of the fund -- including a combined 44.4% in the six "Magnificent Seven" stocks that are underperforming the Nasdaq-100 YTD.

Investing in leading Nasdaq and NYSE growth stocks

The Mega Cap Growth ETF is a great buy for investors who believe today's most valuable companies will continue leading the broader market over the long term. But some investors may lean toward buying a Nasdaq-100 index ETF, such as the popular Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ), rather than the Mega Cap Growth ETF. The issue with that strategy is twofold.

For starters, the Invesco QQQ Trust has a relatively high expense ratio of 0.18%. And, more importantly, it invests exclusively in Nasdaq-listed non-financial companies -- meaning it excludes key growth stocks listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

title: Elon Musk's $474 Million Election Bet Backfires
detail:
Elon Musk's $474 Million Election Bet Backfires
Moz Farooque ACCA
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 12:51 PM MST 2 min read
TSLA
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) and SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) shares fell roughly 4% to 5% Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, creating fresh political and regulatory uncertainty around Elon Musk's companies.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

TSLA GF Value chart

The election outcome is particularly notable because Musk spent nearly $474 million during the election cycle, primarily backing Republicans and conservative political groups. Despite that spending, Democrats scored a broad victory that could give congressional committees more power to investigate Musk's government relationships and businesses.

SpaceX may face the most direct exposure.

The company has extensive federal contracts tied to Starlink, Starshield and U.S. defense programs. Democratic lawmakers have previously called for greater scrutiny of Musk's government work, military communications arrangements and federal contracting relationships. Committee control could potentially mean more hearings, subpoenas and oversight, although it would not automatically cancel existing contracts.

Tesla faces a different set of risks.

Lawmakers could intensify scrutiny around autonomous-driving safety, robotaxi regulation and potential conflicts involving Musk's government and commercial roles. The election outcome could also complicate a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination, although Congress itself cannot simply veto a private merger.

Another emerging issue is AI infrastructure.

The new political landscape could strengthen efforts to impose tougher requirements on large data centers over electricity demand, water consumption and local infrastructure costs. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has called for tighter restrictions on new data-center projects, including ending certain tax breaks and requiring stronger community protections.

That could matter for SpaceX's rapidly expanding AI-compute ambitions.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest issue is not that Musk backed the losing side of an election.

It is that his political involvement may now translate into higher regulatory risk for his companies.

SpaceX depends heavily on government contracts. Tesla needs favorable treatment around autonomous vehicles, infrastructure and permitting. And Musk's broader AI ambitions require massive amounts of power, land and capital.

A more confrontational Congress could create delays, investigations and added uncertainty even if no major contracts are actually canceled.

Rocket Lab Falls 4%, SpaceX Down 4% as Midterms Make Musk the "Biggest Loser" ©U.S. Air Force photo by Trevor Cokley and kb group via Canva
Key Takeaways

Rocket Lab shares fell 4% after Democrats swept Tuesday's midterms and the backlash against Elon Musk spread across space stocks.

AST SpaceMobile and Planet Labs fell with SpaceX, though Rocket Lab is a SpaceX rival.

Analysts expect Rocket Lab's revenue to nearly triple from 2025 to 2028, and the election doesn't change that.

The bigger test is Rocket Lab's Nov. 9 report, where investors want a Neutron launch date.

Rocket Lab (RKLB:NASDAQ) fell 4% today as the backlash against Elon Musk after Tuesday's Democratic sweep hit SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) and spilled across space stocks.

SpaceX fell 4% on worries that a Democratic Congress will dig into Musk's federal contracts. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) dropped 4%, and Planet Labs (PL:NYSE) fell 6%.

George Noble, who is short SpaceX and Tesla, summed up the mood on X: "Elon Musk is the biggest loser in the elections tonight."

Rocket Lab is a SpaceX rival

That makes Rocket Lab an odd stock to dump: it competes with SpaceX for launches and government work, which a Congress leaning on Musk's contracts could send its way.

And second-quarter revenue rose 62% from a year earlier to $234.1 million.

Analysts expect revenue to climb from $602 million in 2025 to $1.74 billion in 2028:

Rocket Lab (RKLB): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Nothing in Tuesday's results gives them a reason to cut those numbers.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Rocket Lab, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Rocket Lab's Analyst Ratings

AST and Planet face different questions

AST SpaceMobile buys launches from SpaceX and competes with Starlink for phone service, and today SpaceX signed a Qualcomm deal for Starlink Mobile. In August, AST said it was on track for $150 million to $200 million of 2026 revenue. It also reports Nov. 9: can it date its next BlueBird launches?

Planet faces a different worry: government budgets. Its revenue rose 58% to $116.1 million in the quarter ended July 31, and in August it won awards from the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and the German government. Does that keep coming under the new Congress's first budget?

Nov. 9 matters more than Tuesday

Rocket Lab reports third-quarter results after the close on Monday, Nov. 9, and investors want a date: Neutron's first launch slipped into 2027 on Oct. 14, and the company didn't give one.

And the stock isn't cheap. It traded at 28x forward sales at the last close (a bit less after today's drop), against a five-year average of 21x:
